sections.html:
Louisa is a rural central Virginia county roughly an hour or less from Richmond, Fredericksburg and Charlottesville. The town of Louisa is the seat, and Mineral is the only other incorporated town. Population was 20,325 in 1990 and 37,596 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 42,924, more than double in thirty-five years. Retirees settling near Lake Anna and commuters drive much of that growth.

A vacancy rate that high means plenty of empty houses, and about a fifth of residents are 65 or older, so estates and downsizing sales are part of the local picture.

State practice splits the job: the county Treasurer mails bills and collects, while a separate assessing office sets values. Call the Treasurer's office and the county's real estate office in Louisa for current dates and figures, and ask for these items in writing:

  • Your current balance, with penalty and interest broken out
  • The next due date and the last day to pay without penalty
  • The deadline and form for appealing an assessment
  • Whether the property is enrolled in a land use or relief program that could affect a sale

For an estate sale, also ask what documents the county wants when a personal representative signs.

The county governing body may by resolution allow reasonable extensions of up to 90 days on real estate tax when good cause exists, and the official who grants one must keep a record. Anyone in the armed forces deployed abroad gets an automatic extension on a primary residence, lasting until 90 days after the deployment ends.

If omitted taxes are assessed, the locality may let the Treasurer set up a payment agreement of no more than 72 months, as long as current taxes are paid when due. Ask the Treasurer which of these options Louisa uses.

State law limits what a county can do to a late payer. The most a county can charge as a late penalty is 10 percent of the tax past due, and interest starts out capped at 10 percent a year. Several situations remove the penalty altogether:

  • The assessment was made less than two weeks before the due date through the fault of a local official, and it is paid within two weeks of the notice.
  • A payment arrives within five days by mail with a missing or unreadable postmark.
  • The taxpayer shows a Postal Service Certificate of Mailing or other proof of mailing from before the deadline.
  • The taxpayer died or had a medically determinable impairment on the due date, and payment follows within 30 days. A guardian or fiduciary gets 120 days after they begin to act.

Appeals also pause collection. An administrative appeal filed within 90 days of the assessment holds off delinquency while it is pending and for 30 days after the decision. Read the statute at Virginia Code 58.1-3916.

sections.h2: Lake Anna, the 2011 earthquake and inspections
sections.html:
Lake Anna, a 13,000-acre lake, and the North Anna Nuclear Generating Station were built by Virginia Power in the 1970s. A magnitude 5.8 earthquake struck on August 23, 2011, centered about five miles south-southwest of Mineral, and damage in the county topped $70 million, including $11.5 million to residential structures. A buyer's inspector may ask about foundation cracks or chimney repairs on older houses, so keep repair records and receipts together and be honest about past damage.

On a rural lot, learn how water and sewage are handled and whether a community association applies, and have those details ready before a sale. Roads in the area include Interstate 64, U.S. 15, 33, 250 and 522, and State Routes 22, 208 and 231. Louisa County Public Schools serves the whole county as a single division, so one office answers attendance questions.

sections.h2: Where in the county is the house?
sections.html: Louisa's communities are scattered. Beyond the towns of Louisa and Mineral you will find Blue Ridge Shores, Apple Grove, Bumpass, Cuckoo, Ferncliff, Gum Spring, Holly Grove, Orchid, Trevilians, Yanceyville and Zion Crossroads. Buyers coming from Richmond tend to ask about the drive on Interstate 64, while lake shoppers care about water access and dock rights. Describe your address by the community name people actually use, and mention anything unusual about the lot, such as shared roads, wells, septic fields or acreage you can subdivide.

About a fifth of residents are 65 or older, so many Louisa sales follow a death. Start with the paperwork: the deed or will, court papers naming the person with authority to sell, and recent tax bills. Next, ring the Treasurer for the balance. Tax keeps accruing while the heirs decide what to do, and an empty house can carry months of unpaid installments before anyone notices.

The late-payment protections above help a fiduciary. A guardian or personal representative has 120 days after they begin to act, and a taxpayer who died on the due date is presumed not at fault if payment follows within 30 days. Ask the Treasurer how the office applies those rules to your case before you assume a penalty will be waived, and keep copies of every letter.

sections.h2: How tax is split at closing
sections.html:
A mid-period closing leaves it to the contract to say who covers which months. The settlement agent turns that agreement into credits and charges on your statement. Read the line for real estate tax, and ask the agent to show the dates used.

If a bill goes out after the sale, the treasurer may reissue it to the new owner, who then has two weeks from the new notice to pay without penalty. Do not rely on that to skip your own share, because a balance you owe at closing is paid out of your proceeds, along with any penalty and interest added by then.

  1. Ask the Treasurer for the amount owed and its good-through date.
  2. Ask whether a land use or relief program on the parcel changes after the transfer.
  3. Pass the written payoff to the closing agent.
  4. File the receipt that shows the tax paid.

Owners behind on tax, or heirs with a house that needs work, can sell as is for cash and clear the tax balance when they close. An heir who takes over after a death also benefits from the fiduciary rule above, which gives a guardian or personal representative extra time after they qualify.

Cash Home Buyers can review a Louisa County house in any condition, including one near Lake Anna or on acreage, and provide a written cash offer. Accepting is optional; the Treasurer's payoff figure gives you a number to compare. Selling for cash avoids the repair list and the wait on a buyer's financing, a fit for a house with foundation worries or a long vacancy.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Louisa County real estate tax?
faqs.a: Call the county Treasurer for balances and due dates, and the county's real estate office for values. Ask for the balance in writing.

faqs.q: How many people live in Louisa County?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 37,596 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 42,924.

faqs.q: What caused the 2011 earthquake damage in Louisa County?
faqs.a: A magnitude 5.8 earthquake on August 23, 2011, centered about five miles south-southwest of Mineral, caused more than $70 million in damage countywide.

faqs.q: Can a Louisa County tax penalty be waived after a death?
faqs.a: Virginia law presumes the taxpayer was not at fault if payment comes within 30 days of the due date after a death or medical impairment. A fiduciary has 120 days after qualifying.
About 80.3 percent of occupied housing units were owner-occupied in the 2020 census, and 14.7 percent of all units were vacant.
